fatal_errors: The proposed refractory-metal additions are absent from the target Fe–Ni–Co–Mn–Cr–P alloy and do not reconstruct its Fe/Co/Mn/P compositional adjustment.
The cited studies address mechanical properties, crystalline microstructures, or additive manufacturing, not enhancement of glass-forming ability by refractory elements.
The initial state is incorrectly designated as amorphous; the target compares a crystalline arc-melted ingot with a melt-spun amorphous ribbon.

The hypothesis omits the central role of reduced phosphorus, eutectic-dominated solidification, suppression of segregation and phosphide nucleation, and the limited ribbon-scale amorphization boundary.
explanation: The response recognizes only the broad themes of alloying and rapid cooling to improve glass formation. It otherwise proposes a different, unsupported intervention involving W, Mo, Ta, or Nb. It does not identify the target Fe22Ni16Co19Mn12Cr16P15 composition, its comparison with Cr16Mn16Fe16Co16Ni16P20, the 40 m/s melt-spinning condition, the approximately 20 μm ribbon limit, or the eutectic/phosphide mechanism. Its proposed DSC/XRD study could test its own claim at a basic level, but it lacks quantitative compositions, cooling conditions, controls, and glass-forming metrics. Most critically, none of the supplied evidence demonstrates that refractory-metal additions enhance glass-forming ability.
